what: Independent fourth check of the steering additions at 94d946d9 (D22 noise, dev weights 1 and 2, script options, extended comparison, weight rule, docs): two reviewers, each followed by a skeptic.

findings.title: The judged-weight rule fixed before the runs does not say which margin it checks. Read literally, it already rules weight 2 out at the D22 noise, although the docs say weight 2 'sits at the rule'.
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/runs/trike60-steer1-dev_STEPS.md section 5 (the noise-check bullet and the 'judged weight, by this rule' bullet); README 'The weight' bullets, DECISION_LOG D29 and PLAN_STEERING_RUN.md status ('weight 2 sits at the rule (+0.27-0.31)')
findings.evidence:
Source: heat_weight_margins_d22noise_3M_5M.md, which I regenerated exactly from the committed episodes. At policy+0.125, weight 2:
- nominal 0.25 m/s: +0.29 +-0.07
- nominal 0.15 m/s: +0.31 +-0.04
- x1.1 0.25 m/s: +0.27 +-0.07
- x1.1 0.15 m/s: +0.31 +-0.06

So 2 of the 4 cells are under the rule's 0.3, and 'under 0.3 -> out'. Interpolating the worst cells between std 0.11 and 0.125 (0.44 -> 0.29 nominal, 0.38 -> 0.27 x1.1), weight 2 crosses 0.3 at noise 0.124 (nominal) and 0.121 (x1.1). That is at or below the bottom of D22's 0.123-0.128 at 3 M (d22_action_std.json, which I reproduced byte for byte).

The rule leaves open:
- which cells count (nominal or x1.1, which speed, worst of four policies or not);
- what tolerance applies (SE up to 0.07-0.09; the README says figures within about 0.1 are not told apart);
- which noise point (it reads 1, 2 and 3 M).

The sheet says only '--stds <that noise>'. A 2 M check also needs --late 0.5. Without it, the full-scale margin at the 2 M noise 0.147 is about +0.11-0.15 at weight 2, so weight 2 would be wrongly out.

The STEPS figure '+0.11 at 0.15' is nominal only. x1.1 gives +0.04 and +0.05 in heat_weight_margins.md, while D29's +0.27-0.31 range includes x1.1.

'More falls than the other run' with one seed each lets a one-fall difference decide.

Result: whether weight 2 survives turns on unstated details and on noise differences of about 0.003, which biases the choice towards weight 1 or invites reading the rule after the fact.

findings.title: The every-drive reference cost (cost_sum_w1) ignores --late, so the committed heat_weight_margins_every_drive_d22noise_2M.md prices every drive at twice the late-0.5 scale
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/analysis/steer_heat_weight.py lines 78-79 (cost_sum from env._heat_ema with no late_scale); analysis/results/steer1/heat_weight/heat_weight_margins_every_drive_d22noise_2M.md; README 'Pricing every drive ... 2.4-4.1 times as much (heat_weight_margins_every_drive*)'
findings.evidence:
Same 'noise' episodes, late 1 file against the late 0.5 file:
- cost_w1: 0.2102 -> 0.1051.
- r_heat and r_saturation: exactly 0.5x. r_track, r_slip and r_energy: 1.0x, so the trajectories are identical.

findings.title: d22_action_std.py's nearest-row pick ignores resumed sessions and torn lines; it would read a discarded branch on a resumed run's log
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/analysis/d22_action_std.py trajectory() (json.loads on every line, then min over all rows)
findings.evidence:
Synthetic log (check4_steer/synth_health): session A runs to 3.27 M and is killed; session B resumes from 2,752,512 with action_std 0.5. The script returns A's discarded row at 2,998,272 (0.1634) for 3 M; exact ties go to the first row in the file. A torn last line (a run killed mid-write) would make json.loads raise. telemetry/health.py already has read_health and latest_branch for both cases.

The four D22 logs are each a single session with 1221 rows, strictly increasing timesteps and no duplicates. So the committed output is right: I reproduced it byte for byte, and it agrees with linear interpolation to 0.0001. The risk is reusing the script on the dev runs, which are 4.5-5 h on Colab and often resumed.
findings.suggested_fix: Load rows with telemetry.health.read_health followed by latest_branch(rows, 'timesteps'), and refuse when the nearest row is more than one rollout (8192 steps) from the point.

verdicts.reasoning:
The rule written into the step sheet before the runs says a weight is out if 'its noise check above leaves a margin over standing under 0.3'. It does not say:
- which of the script's four cells count (nominal or x1.1, 0.25 or 0.15 m/s);
- whether a standard error or other tolerance applies;
- which noise point counts. The check reads 1, 2 and 3 M, and only the README, not the sheet, ties the rule to 3 M.

At the D22 noise of 0.125, weight 2 is under 0.3 in 2 of its 4 cells, by 0.01-0.03, while the standard errors are 0.04-0.07. So whether weight 2 survives depends on those unstated details. 'Sits at the rule (+0.27-0.31)' is a fair description of 'at the threshold', but the rule as written fails that range. The '+0.11 at 0.15' figure is the nominal cell only.

Running the check at the 2 M noise without --late 0.5 wrongly rules weight 2 out, and the sheet does not warn against that. 'More falls than the other run' names no evaluation and no minimum difference.

Medium, not high: the dev runs themselves are unaffected; this is ambiguity in the pre-registration that picks the judged weight. The noise point is partly resolved by the README's statement that the rule applies at the 3 M noise, but the sheet's own wording invites checks at 1 and 2 M.
verdicts.evidence:
- Committed heat_weight_margins_d22noise_3M_5M.md, policy+0.125, weight 2: nominal 0.25 m/s +0.29 +-0.07; nominal 0.15 m/s +0.31 +-0.04; x1.1 0.25 m/s +0.27 +-0.07; x1.1 0.15 m/s +0.31 +-0.06.
- At policy+0.11, weight 2: nominal 0.25 +0.44, x1.1 0.25 +0.38. The worst policy is the same at both noise levels (s2 nominal, s3 x1.1). Linear interpolation crosses 0.3 at noise 0.1243 (nominal) and 0.1209 (x1.1).

- I ran steer_heat_weight.py myself on fore128-s2 and s3 with --stds 0.147 --late 1 (60 episodes, 0 falls; scratch check4_steer/skeptic/hw147). Weight 2: +0.12, +0.17, +0.10 and +0.09 across the four cells, all under 0.3. Weight 1: +0.38 to +0.42. With --late 0.5, the committed 2M file has weight 2 at +0.50 to +0.55.
- STEPS section 5 says only '--stds <that noise>' after 'at 1, 2 and 3 M'. Its rule bullet names no cells, no tolerance and no evaluation for falls. README line 440 says 'figures within about 0.1 of each other are not told apart'.

verdicts.reasoning:
In episode(), cost_sum is built directly from env._heat_ema with no late scale. cost_w1 comes from info['r_heat_peak'], which does include late_scale. So at --late 0.5 the every-drive reference is priced at full scale while everything else is at half scale.

The committed _d22noise_2M every-drive table is therefore wrong. The hottest-drive tables are correct. No decision rests on the wrong table, but the README's 'heat_weight_margins_every_drive*' pointer covers it, and the code is wrong for any --late below 1.

findings.title: The step sheet's noise exclusion for weight 2 is undefined, and at the expected noise it flips on a few thousandths of noise
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/runs/trike60-steer1-dev_STEPS.md section 5 (bullets 2 and 4); rl/README.md 'Weight 2 needs the noise near the D22 figure' and 'weight 2 sits at the rule'; PLAN status; DECISION_LOG D29
findings.evidence: I ran steer_heat_weight.py myself on all four D22 128 mm policies at late 1. For weight 2, the worst-of-four margins (nominal 0.25 / nominal 0.15 / x1.1 0.25 / x1.1 0.15 m/s) were: noise 0.12: +0.37 / +0.43 / +0.31 / +0.33, all four pass. Noise 0.125 (the committed table, which I reproduced byte for byte): +0.29 / +0.31 / +0.27 / +0.31, two of four under 0.3. Noise 0.13: +0.25 / +0.34 / +0.26 / +0.25, three of four under. The 0.15 m/s cell does not even move steadily with noise (0.43, 0.31, 0.34), and its standard errors are 0.04-0.08. The D22 runs' 3 M noise, 0.1230-0.1282, sits right on this cut (about 0.12-0.125). The rule says 'a weight is out if its noise check leaves a margin over standing under 0.3', but it does not say: (a) which policies are used. The default --runs is the four D22 straight-task policies. Yet the README says that table 'predicts nothing' for steering, and the dev runs' own 5 M policies are never named. (b) Which of the noises read at 1, 2 and 3 M goes into --stds, or at what --late. The sheet gives --stds only, so late defaults to 1. At late 1 the 2 M noise of about 0.147 gives weight 2 about +0.11 (the 0.15 row), but the README's 2 M check uses --late 0.5 and gets +0.54-0.55. (c) Which cells count, and which statistic (worst policy or mean; nominal or x1.1; one speed or both). Read most strictly (worst cell), weight 2 is OUT at the D22 noise. That contradicts 'sits at the rule' in README, PLAN and D29, and the sheet's 'sits at the margin rule only if the noise at 3 M is near 0.123-0.128': at 0.128-0.13 it fails. So whether weight 2 survives depends on unstated reading choices and on measurement scatter, not on what the weight-2 run does.
findings.suggested_fix: Before the runs, fix the check in section 5. Use the four D22 policies (default --runs), each dev run's action_std at the rollout nearest 3,000,000 steps, and --late 1 (and, if wanted, the 2 M noise at --late 0.5). Name the statistic, for example the worst-of-four mean at nominal 0.25 and 0.15 m/s. Put a tolerance on it that matches the standard errors, or turn the test into a noise threshold read off the measured rows now (for example: weight 2 is out if the 3 M noise is over 0.125, weight 1 if over 0.16). Say plainly that at the D22 noise (0.125-0.128) weight 2 is at or just below the line, so it survives only if r_heat_peak lowers the noise.

findings.title: The rest of the judged-weight rule names no measurements, lets one fall decide, and leaves a single surviving weight to inference
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/runs/trike60-steer1-dev_STEPS.md section 5, 'The judged weight, by this rule, fixed before the runs'
findings.evidence: (1) 'more falls than the other run ... at 5 M' does not say which measurement counts: gait report, sweep, steer_eval courses or demo course. The D22 128 mm gait reports read 'falls 0 + 0 of 10 (sweep: 0 falls in 21 episodes)' for all four seeds (analytics/results/fore128-s*/gait_report.md). So one fall in any of these tools rules a weight out. Meanwhile the same rule treats hottest-drive differences under 0.1 as seed noise. (2) 'forward speed at a 0.25 m/s request under 0.2 m/s' does not name the case or statistic; the gait report's randomised target case is presumably meant (D22: 0.235-0.244). (3) The selection clauses compare two weights; the case where exactly one weight is left is covered only by inference. (4) The likely case is both weights over 0.85 (D22 worst drives 0.83, 0.89, 0.93, 0.95). If they are also within 0.1 of each other, the rule picks weight 1, the weight least likely to meet the planned judged heat rule (worst drive under about 0.85), and does not go back to the owner. (5) The 0.85 clause picks on any difference that straddles 0.85 (for example 0.84 against 0.86), although the sheet says differences under 0.1 are seed spread.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the measurement for each criterion. For example: falls = total over the sweep's and the gait report's episodes, out only if at least 2 more than the other run; speed = the gait report's 0.25 m/s randomised case. Add 'if one weight is left, that one'. Decide now what happens when both weights are over 0.85 (the higher weight, or back to the owner). Consider a band on the 0.85 clause (for example, only if the other run is at least 0.05 over 0.85).

findings.title: PLAN still gives the 0.80-0.82 price share without its qualifier; PLAN and D29 quote the D22 noise as 'on the same schedules' and leave out the differences between the tasks
findings.location: hardware/triceratops_build/rl/PLAN_STEERING_RUN.md status bullet 3 ('which weights every step alike and prices 0.80-0.82 of F2's own price') and bullet 4; DECISION_LOG D29; rl/README.md 'The weight' bullets; analysis/d22_action_std.py docstring

The steer1 presets are flat (D28), 0-20 ms, x0.9-1.1, 0-1 kg, heading_and_speed. train.py's schedule defaults are the same (I checked), so 'same schedules' is true. findings.suggested_fix: In PLAN, write 'prices 0.80-0.82 of F2's price on gaits well over the margin (1.26 on the coolest group)'. In PLAN, D29 and the README, add one clause: the D22 runs trained the straight task with terrain from 1 M, 0-10 ms delays and no whole-robot draws or r_heat_peak, so their noise is a guide only. findings.title: The 0.3 rule's operating point moved from the initial noise 0.2 to the 3 M noise; the move is sound but presented as a simple application

verdicts.reasoning: I re-ran steer_heat_weight.py at noise 0.12 and 0.13 (late 1, default D22 runs) and got the reviewer's numbers exactly. Weight 2's worst-of-four margins sit right on 0.3 across the D22 3 M noise range (0.123-0.128), and they move by more than their standard errors for 0.005 changes in noise. The committed 0.125 table already gives +0.29 in the headline cell (nominal, 0.25 m/s). So under the README's own cell statistic, weight 2 is out at the D22 noise. That conflicts with 'sits at the rule' and with the sheet's 'sits at the margin rule only if the noise at 3 M is near 0.123-0.128'. Sub-point (b) holds. The sheet asks for the noise at 1, 2 and 3 M with only '--stds <that noise>'. At the default late 1, the 2 M noise gives +0.11, as the sheet itself quotes. The README's own 2 M check used --late 0.5 (+0.54-0.55). At 1 M the late scale is 0, so a check at late 1 makes no sense there. Sub-point (c) holds: no cell, speed, condition or statistic is named for 'a margin under 0.3'. Sub-point (a) is weaker: the script's default --runs (the four D22 policies) does define which policies are used, so that part is a tension with 'predicts nothing' rather than an undefined input. On the whole, whether weight 2 survives depends on how the rule is read and on scatter, not on the run. That is a real defect in a rule fixed before the runs. It is medium, not high, because the judged runs have their own reviewed pre-registration.

With one weight left, the wording collapses to that weight: it is either 'the only one under 0.85', or 'the higher'/'the lower' both name it. Only stylistic clarity is missing. (4) Holds as a gap. PLAN line 84 plans a judged heat rule of 'the worst drive under a margin below its rating (for example 0.85)'. If both dev weights are over 0.85 and within 0.1 of each other, the rule picks weight 1 and returns to the owner only when both are 'out'. This is mitigated by the reviewed pre-registration that follows. (5) Holds: the 0.85 clause decides on a straddle of any size (0.84 vs 0.86), which contradicts the sheet's own 0.1 seed-spread statement.
